result.summary: This PR extracts and shares the logic that rebuilds a block template for an arbitrary parent (used by BuildChain and MinerTestingSetup::Block) into a single RebuildBlockForParent helper, fixing three latent test-helper bugs: a stale work target, a stale coinbase subsidy, and an unpadded low-height coinbase script that would violate the minimum length. None of the current callers trigger these bugs, so no existing test currently fails; the change is preventative hardening for future test cases.
result.problem: Test helpers that attach active-tip block templates to arbitrary parents copy fields (work target, subsidy, script length) that describe the wrong block once the parent changes, which would silently produce invalid test blocks for any future test that crosses a halving, retargets, or forks below height 17. This affects Bitcoin Core contributors writing new validation/mining-related functional or unit tests using these helpers.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp: using assignment instead of adjustment for the coinbase output means fees present in the original mempool-templated block are dropped; not yet hit by any test but real, suggested using .use_mempool=false at the call site instead as a simpler fix.

jeanpablojp: proposed two additional unit tests (rebuild_block_for_parent_target, rebuild_block_for_parent_coinbase) to cover the new nBits/subsidy/padding logic that currently has no direct test coverage; removing any of the three new lines still leaves existing suites green.
